contentSections: Quick answer

A good shop front elevation design does three jobs: it is noticed from the street, it tells customers what kind of shop this is, and it lasts through Indian sun, dust and monsoon without looking tired. Aluminium and metal cladding suit this well because they can be cut, folded, perforated and coated in many colours while staying light. Metaguise installed systems typically cost about INR 800 to 2,500 per sq ft, depending on system and complexity.
Key takeaways

• Design the front for the person walking by at speed, then for the person standing at the door. • Use two or three materials at most. Metal, glass and a calm backdrop panel is a reliable mix. • Plan signage and lighting with the facade, not after it. • The finish decides how long the shop front looks new. Ask for the written coating warranty.
Why the shop front matters more than the interior

For most small and mid-size retailers, the front elevation is the only advertisement that works every hour the shop is open. Customers decide in a few seconds whether to walk in. Our article on retail facade design covers the larger brand-store view. This guide is for the single shop, showroom or small commercial unit where the front is a few hundred square feet.
Start with proportion, then material

Our guide to front elevation design ideas explains proportion in detail. For shops, the same principles apply with a commercial twist: the entrance should be the clearest element, the signage should have a defined zone, and the upper floor should support the brand without competing with it.
A simple order of decisions works well:
1. Entrance and door position 2. Signage zone 3. Main cladding material and colour 4. Accent material 5. Lighting 6. Security and shutters
Metal cladding ideas for a shop front
Flat aluminium panels with hairline joints

A clean backdrop that makes products and signage stand out. Suited to clothing, electronics, clinics and offices. Joint detail matters here, because flat panels show every misalignment. See SolidPanel.
Fluted or linear panels
Vertical lines add height and rhythm, and catch light through the day. Good for food outlets, salons and boutiques.
Perforated screens

A perforated layer in front of a plain wall or glass gives depth and shade, and can carry a pattern linked to your brand. Hole size and open area change how the screen looks by day and by night, covered in our guide to perforated metal panel design.
Textured modules
Circular or faceted modules create a feature wall behind the entrance. They suit shops that want a signature look, such as jewellery and gifting.
Warm metal accents
Brass, copper or bronze-toned finishes on frames, canopies and nameplates add warmth. Some metals change colour with time, so decide whether you want that patina.

Lighting and signage

Warm light at about 2700K to 3000K flatters most metal tones. Graze light from above across the cladding to show texture, and avoid spotlights that cause glare on glass. Fixtures should be rated for outdoor use, ideally IP65 or better. Integrate the shop name into the cladding with cut letters, raised metal lettering or a backlit panel, and plan cables and fixings at the design stage so finished panels are not drilled later. How much does a shop front elevation cost?

Metaguise installed systems typically fall between INR 800 and INR 2,500 per sq ft, depending on system and complexity. For a 600 sq ft shop front, that is roughly INR 4.8 lakh to INR 15 lakh for cladding only. Lighting, glass, signage and shutters are priced separately.

What moves the price: custom modules, special finishes, building height and access equipment, and integrated lighting. Small projects under 500 sq ft carry higher proportional costs. For a full explanation, read our guide to metal facade cladding cost in India. These figures are indicative and not a quotation.
Mistakes that make a shop front look cheaper than the stock inside

• Too many materials and colours on a small front • Signage as an afterthought, stuck on top of finished cladding • Cheap coating that fades within two or three seasons • No plan for festive lighting, so holes are drilled later • Ignoring the shutter, which is closed for half of every day
Frequently asked questions

1. What is the best material for shop front elevation design?

Coated aluminium is the most common choice because it is light, easy to shape and available in many finishes. The best option depends on the shop type and budget.

2. What does aluminium front elevation design cost per square foot?

Metaguise installed systems typically fall between INR 800 and INR 2,500 per sq ft depending on system and complexity. Ask for a project-specific quotation.

3. Can metal sheet be used for a front elevation?

Yes. Aluminium sheet is cut and formed into flat, folded, fluted or perforated panels. Panel thickness and fixing depend on size and wind exposure.

4. How long does a shop front last?

It depends on the finish and care. Premium coatings carry long warranties, and regular washing keeps the surface in good condition.

5. Do I need approval for a new shop front?

Rules differ by city and building. Check with your local authority and landlord before starting.
